pr_title: usb: bluetooth: do not start transfers when USB bus is suspended
pr_body:
Do not start transfers when USB bus is suspended.
If the bus is suspended, initiate remote-wakeup and
wait until the bus is operational.

Allow to disable option USB_DEVICE_REMOTE_WAKEUP.

Fixes: #40776
pr_comments:
>As we are in a while loop, without suspended being quailified as volatile would mean a register storage will be used and no fresh memory access will happen, potentially causing a deadlock in this while loop.

I simply cannot agree with that. Why should suspended become register storage-class specifier without volatile and by whom? Why should this thread when it sleeps prevent others from updating memory? Rather, it could happen that _not updated_ suspended == true condition will be unnoticed.

>Use of semaphore signal on change to suspended will avoid an upto 1 ms latency in the USB transport on wakeup.

1 ms is minimum expected resume time (resume signaling TDRSMUP 1ms .. 15ms + some recovery time), here on average (1 root hub in between) of 5ms, and then it does not mean that controller event arrives immediately by the host.

> Why should suspended become register storage-class specifier without volatile and by whom

Atleast in ARM, arithmetic and logic operations are performed as register operands

> Why should this thread when it sleeps prevent others from updating memory?

The sleep does not prevent the updating of memory, but on resumption in the loop then the updated memory shall be loaded into register everytime.

`suspended` being global and the loop having a function should make the compiler generate code to reload `suspended` everytime, but using the `volatile` qualifier make implementation explicit, see for example when the function is not present then there is no reload (of r3 register) in the generated code:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6350656/144462736-99334fcd-ffe0-4f22-87dd-ba00423cb382.png)

Now with volatile added:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6350656/144463451-0f21ee5e-0f66-4cfb-93ab-5b22638b0eec.png)

> > Why should suspended become register storage-class specifier without volatile and by whom
> 
> Atleast in ARM, arithmetic and logic operations are performed as register operands

That is not what I mean.

> > Why should this thread when it sleeps prevent others from updating memory?
> 
> The sleep does not prevent the updating of memory, but on resumption in the loop then the updated memory shall be loaded into register everytime.
> 
> `suspended` being global and the loop having a function should make the compiler generate code to reload `suspended` 

suspended has static storage-class specifier, no side effects, no mem based io.

>everytime, but using the `volatile` qualifier make implementation explicit, see for example when the function is not present then there is no reload (of r3 register) in the generated code: ...
> 
> Now with volatile added: ...

I am not sure what you are comparing, but it is more than:
```diff
diff --git a/subsys/usb/class/bluetooth.c b/subsys/usb/class/bluetooth.c
index b6a93012fbd..eee1e7dbd09 100644
--- a/subsys/usb/class/bluetooth.c
+++ b/subsys/usb/class/bluetooth.c
@@ -42,7 +42,7 @@ static struct k_thread tx_thread_data;
 
 /* HCI USB state flags */
 static bool configured;
-volatile static bool suspended;
+static bool suspended;
 
 static uint8_t ep_out_buf[USB_MAX_FS_BULK_MPS];
```
With arm-none-eabi-gcc 10.3.1, I do not see any difference, with or without volatile. Of course, it can be different with other compilers, but IMHO unlikely with modern compilers and this code.

The comparison is " the function is not present " in side the while loop. in C99 standard (if my memory serves right), compiler assumes that global variable could be modified by an external function inside the loop, hence you do not see the difference between volatile and no volatile, but as soon as compiler is able to see the contents of the function inside the while loop it can take a decision not to load the register from memory.

issue_context.title: HCI_USB with nRF52840 dongle disconnect after 30 s
issue_context.body:
Hi,

**Describe the bug**

I try to connect simultaneous 12 BLE devices to a Linux PC with Bluez.
Commercial controllers cannot go beyond 5 connections. I am using an nRF52840 dongle.

I use the hci_usb sample flashed by dfu.

On the PC, the 12 connections are made without problems with bluetoothctl.
Only after about 30s, a device disconnects.
It is not necessarily the same and it is possible to reconnect afterwards but this disconnection is a problem for my application.

It is not at the level of the devices, nor of the bluetoothctl commands since everything works with a commercial BLE controller (only for 5 devices).

Before the disconnection, the bluetoothctl "info" command line indicates that the device is connected and displays the list of all BLE services. 

I also tested with the nRF52832 DK board and the hci_uart example for the same result.

Is there a way to solve this problem? 

**Logs and console output**

With btmon, I get the disconnection reason : Remote User Terminated Connection
HCI Command: Disconnect (0x01|0x0006) plen 3                                            
        Handle: 0
        Reason: Remote User Terminated Connection (0x13)

**Environment:**

OS: Linux Mint, bluez 
Toolchain: Zephyr SDK: Zephyr from master or v2.7.99.

**Additional context**

None
comments: I can confirm it, but did not had time to investigate, it is somehow related to USB device support. zephyr-v2.7.0 does not seem to be affected.

As it is Remote User Terminated Connection, I suspect a ATT request that was not delivered to the host BT stack or a response from the host BT stack did not reach the remote peer, which then  initiated the disconnect on the 30s ATT transaction timeout.

Thank for your replies.

I try with zephyr-v2.7.0 version and it is exactly the same behavior with a disconnection on 12 after 30s.
For hci_usb and hci_uart.

I also tried a multitude of different configuration for prj.conj but without success.

> I try with zephyr-v2.7.0 version and it is exactly the same behavior with a disconnection on 12 after 30s.

Please recheck, zephyr-v2.7.0 works fine.

git bisect shows 02c32d44746be8c2f45bcea375dfe37693ee5ae3 as cause. Host periodically requests Set Feature DEVICE_REMOTE_WAKEUP, suspends, resumes, requests Clear Feature; corresponding suspend/resume logic in _subsys/usb/class/bluetooth.c_ seems to have a bug.

I recheck, I got the same behaviour again with v2.7.0 even with a different Linux PC.
One in 12 devices is disconnected 30 s after the first connection with the reason : Remote User Terminated Connection (0x13).
This device is connected a few seconds later and then there is no disconnection ever again.

You are right, that's work with v2.7.0. 
My problem is due to an overflow on BLE stack.
When I wait a successful connection before launching another, I no longer have a disconnection.
Thank you for your time and contribution.

review_comments:
Concerns:
1. Polling introduces upto 1 ms (33 RTC ticks of 32KHz clock) latency on resume.
2. USB suspend state maintained in Bluetooth code.
3. Drawback that USB interface does not provide means to use OS synchronization to wake up thread on state change, may be there is a USB state query and callback interface that could be used for thread resume.
